translation:
  text: '“The believers from the first mountain, the black one, are like this: they are apostates, blasphemers
    against the Lord, and betrayers of God’s servants. Repentance is not available to them, but death
    is. That is also why they are black, for their kind is lawless.”


    2. “The believers from the second mountain, the bare one,[a] are like this: they are hypocrites and
    teachers of evil. They too resemble the former people, bearing no fruit of righteousness. Just as
    their mountain bears no fruit, these people have a name, but are empty of faith, and there is no fruit
    of truth in them. Repentance is available to them, then, if they repent quickly. But if they delay,
    they will die along with the former people.”


    3. “Why, sir,” I said, “is repentance available to these people but not to the former ones? Their
    actions are almost the same.”[b] “Repentance is available to these people,” he said, “because they
    did not blaspheme their Lord or become betrayers of God’s servants. Their desire for gain led them
    to act hypocritically, and each taught according to the desires of people who were sinning.[c] But
    they will pay some penalty. Repentance is available to them because they did not become blasphemers
    or betrayers.”'
  philosophy: optimal-equivalence
  footnotes:

    text: '“Bare” follows Anger’s printed conjecture compared with Latin Vulgata. The apparatus reports
      Athos and Ethiopic “high,” and Latin Palatina “dry.” Alternatives: “The believers from the second
      mountain, the high one” or “the dry one.” The following fruitlessness is retained under each choice.'
  - marker: b
    reason: textual_variant
    text: “Former ones” translates προτέροις, Hilgenfeld’s printed conjecture compared with the Latin
      and Ethiopic versions; the apparatus reports Athos πρώτοις (“first ones”). “The same” translates
      αἱ αὐταί, Anger’s printed conjecture compared with those versions; the apparatus reports Athos καὶ
      αὗται (“and these”). These reported alternatives are not reconstructed here as a complete clause.
      The near-equivalence is Hermas’s question, not a denial of the shepherd’s following distinction.
  - marker: c
    reason: textual_variant
    text: “According to” translates a bracketed insertion in the printed source, absent from Athos as
      reported. Desire for gain, the continuing penalty, and the stated difference between available and
      unavailable repentance remain explicit.
